subject: Brown algae
hook: BROWN ALGAE IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK
angle: Brown algae aren't plants at all – they belong to the SAR supergroup (Stramenopiles) and are only distantly related to green plants, red algae, and true algae
angle_support: "Brown algae belong to the Stramenopiles, a clade of eukaryotic organisms belonging to the SAR supergroup, and are thus not closely related to red algae, green algae, nor green plants (which are all archaeplastids)."
"Brown algae (sing.: alga) are a large group of photoautotrophic, multicellular SAR comprising the class Phaeophyceae."
title: Brown Algae Aren’t Plants – They’re SAR Supergroup Relatives
description: Most viewers assume kelp and seaweed are just plant cousins. In fact, brown algae sit in the SAR supergroup, far removed from true plants. Their unique four‑membrane chloroplasts reveal a separate evolutionary path.
narration: BROWN ALGAE IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK You think brown algae are just sea plants, cousins of green lettuce. In reality they belong to the SAR supergroup, distant from true plants and other algae that thrive in cold, nutrient‑rich seas. Brown algae belong to the class Phaeophyceae, part of the Stramenopiles lineage, which is outside the Archaeplastida that holds green plants and red algae. Their chloroplasts have four membranes, showing secondary endosymbiosis and proves they’re distant from true plants. So the kelp forest is a distant cousin, not a plant, truly a SAR member.
